about.title: TechWire — articles on development, economics and science
about.lead: A publication for people who write code and want to understand what is going on around it: technology deep dives, plain explanations, and material that is still useful a week later.

it.name: Development
it.text: Frontend and backend, tools and approaches: React and Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind, state managers, Go, Rust, Python. Walkthroughs with real code, not a retelling of the docs.

economics.name: Economics
economics.text: How the money around technology works: product unit economics, inflation and rates, investing, cryptocurrencies and how to store them.

science.name: Science
science.text: Big topics in plain language: the James Webb telescope, CRISPR genome editing, quantum computing, black holes.

about.stackText: The project runs on React 18 and TypeScript, organised with Feature-Sliced Design: the code is split into layers from shared UI primitives up to pages, and each layer only knows about the ones below it. Application state is Redux Toolkit; server data is RTK Query, with caching and tag-based invalidation. Webpack 5 handles bundling, with code splitting per route.
about.ctaText: Over 30 pieces on development, economics and science — with real code and no filler.
about.principlesLead: This is not a feed of reworded press releases. Every piece goes through four rules, and they are what separates this from a news aggregator.

practice.name: Practice, not paraphrase
practice.text: We do not rewrite the docs in our own words. A piece explains what problem the technology solves, where it wins and what it costs you — with examples you can actually run.

depth.name: Explain the mechanism
depth.text: "It is faster" is not an explanation. We go into why: how the algorithm works, what happens at runtime, which trade-offs are baked into the design.

honest.name: Honest trade-offs
honest.text: Every choice has a price. If a tool is convenient but locks you into an ecosystem or falls apart at scale, we say so plainly instead of listing only its strengths.

lasting.name: Built to last
lasting.text: We pick topics that will still be useful in a year: principles, architectural approaches and fundamentals. The hype around the latest release is someone else's beat.

learning.name: People still learning
learning.text: If you know your way around frontend or backend and are tired of build-a-counter tutorials, here are real problems worked through, with the reasoning behind the code.

working.name: Working developers
working.text: Comparisons of tools and approaches, so that "what should we use" rests on understanding the trade-offs rather than on the first search result.

curious.name: The simply curious
curious.text: Economics and science without formulas or jargon: how inflation works, what James Webb found, why quantum error correction matters.

about.stackText2: Quality rests on three levels of checking: unit tests in Jest and Testing Library, end-to-end journeys in a real browser via Playwright, and static analysis — TypeScript, ESLint, Stylelint and an architectural-boundary linter. It is a production-style learning project: the UI, the architecture and the tests are working code, not a mock-up.
